title: LLMs, world models, and what comes next
userDirection: Explain where intelligence goes next, how language models and different world-model functions coexist, and why domain-specific prediction matters. Preserve the author’s concise personal tone, avoid em dashes and colons in visible prose, replace the simulator/digital-twin table and rigid model-per-site proposal with explanatory figures, and cite only important sources. The first section is Frontier foundation models. Within it, the frontier-scale SSL/foundation/LLM/omni progression comes first. Long-horizon digital agents follow as systems built on that base intelligence, with further scaling through RL and OPD. That entire section omits world-model discussion. World models are introduced only in a separate following section. The domain-adaptation section compares V-JEPA 2-AC, JEPA-Anything and AD-LiST-JEPA in a concise animated figure and explains why each was selected. The OPF question was a clarification request. Keep the published prose focused on one short paragraph explaining why the three papers were selected together, with the animated comparison retained.

editorialNotes: Retitled around LLMs, world models and where intelligence goes next; retained the original stable URL and publication date and added an explicit 9 October update date for new work including RoboJEPA.

The Forbes council article remains in the references as an inspiration rather than empirical evidence. At the author’s request, removed the opening inspiration paragraph naming Yifeng Yin and Fei-Fei Li and led with the impact of LLMs and long-horizon agents on digital work.
Fei-Fei Li and World Labs are not characterized as pixel-only. Their account includes multimodal, implicit/explicit state and rendering, simulation and planning functions.

Removed the old simulator/digital-twin table, RAG self-citation, old mandatory one-model-per-site architecture and separate checklist. Important challenges now appear briefly beside the proposed composition.
The feedback loop is conditional. User interactions do not automatically retrain a model, and useful examples require evaluation before training and measurement afterwards.
General software-task progress is grounded in METR time horizons defined against human task completion time, without claiming generalized reliability or AGI.

Cosmos 3 and Odyssey-3 can supply policies/actions as well as scenarios. Cosmos 3 includes a 4B Edge variant. Large-lab advantage is an explicitly personal economic hypothesis, not a deterministic architectural claim.

Generative models may operate on compressed latents internally. The distinction is the prediction target and consumer, not the presence of a latent representation or a rigid generative-versus-JEPA taxonomy.

JEPA prediction does not by itself guarantee small models, data efficiency or real-time control. RoboJEPA reaches an 8B predictor and reports seconds-long multi-GPU planning while also decoding latent futures into video.

V-JEPA 2-AC demonstrates a frozen encoder with a learned action-conditioned predictor. The article avoids treating predictor size as full-stack size or adaptation data as total pretraining requirements.

JEPA-Anything uses a shared learning principle across domain-specific adapters/encoders/targets, not one proven universal pretrained checkpoint. Representation learning is distinguished from retaining a predictor for operational dynamics.

The LiDAR source establishes occupancy completion/forecasting evidence, not an action-conditioned driving controller. Other sensor panels are explicit design possibilities, not existing complete systems.

A planner evaluates predicted consequences against a goal. A world model does not inherently supply utility, and the controller executes actions. Potential errors and runtime requirements remain relevant.
Authored visible prose and figure text contain no em dashes or colons. Reference labels are concise descriptive titles linked to their exact sources.

At the author’s request, Frontier foundation models is the first main section. From self-supervised learning to omni models and General models, longer work are subsections within it, in that order. A transition connects long-horizon agents to the underlying base intelligence. World models and their main approaches follows as a separate main section. Existing section anchors remain valid.

The foundation-model section and figure strictly omit world models. They emphasize frontier-scale datasets, model size and compute without asserting all foundation or omni models must be large. LLMs and omni models are identified as foundation-model forms.

Five figures now explain frontier foundation models, evaluated post-training feedback, two overlapping world-model groupings, a possible combined system, and three complementary domain-adaptation papers. Generative/spatial and latent predictive models are discussion groupings, not an exhaustive or mutually exclusive taxonomy.

RL is described as learning from task rewards. OPD is expanded as on-policy distillation, where the student generates trajectories and a teacher provides guidance on those trajectories. These are distinct feedback mechanisms and neither is claimed to improve automatically or to eliminate reliability problems.

Redrew Different jobs, one system to make the LLM, generative/spatial world models and latent predictive world models explicit. Labeled request and return paths connect both world-model branches to shared planning, followed by control and observed feedback. Generated scenarios can support policy development or planning; action-conditioned latent predictions inform decisions when runtime permits. The figure is a possible composition, not a demonstrated universal architecture, and does not require every model to run for every action.

Re-read the three primary papers for the domain-adaptation revision. Figure 05 explains the selection rationale through reuse, prediction structure and sensor-specific learning. All three summaries remain visible; motion traces predictive flow, respects reduced-motion preferences and can be paused with the site-wide motion control. Existing publication and section anchors remain stable.

At the author’s request, replaced the JEPA-Anything methods and assessment paragraphs and the longer conclusion with one concise collective selection rationale. Kept the three-paper figure and its citations.

sources.title: Yifeng Yin. Why Do We Need World Models When LLMs Exist? How World Models Will Impact Physical AI
sources.supportedClaim: Attributed inspiration for LLM/world-model coexistence. Council opinion, not primary experimental evidence.

sources.title: Fei-Fei Li. From Words to Worlds: Spatial Intelligence is AI’s Next Frontier
sources.supportedClaim: Spatial intelligence linking perception, imagination and action; broader than pixel-only prediction.

sources.title: World Labs. A Functional Taxonomy of World Models
sources.supportedClaim: Rendering, simulation and planning are overlapping functional roles, including structural state and not only rendered pixels.

sources.title: METR. Task-Completion Time Horizons of Frontier AI Models
sources.supportedClaim: Growing horizons on evaluated software tasks, with task duration measured against human experts.

sources.title: NVIDIA. Cosmos 3
sources.supportedClaim: Unified generation/reasoning/action capabilities and policy output, compressed video latents, and model family including 4B Edge. These do not establish every variant can meet every physical system’s latency requirements.

sources.title: Oliver Cameron and Jeff Hawke. Introducing Odyssey-3: A General-Purpose Physical Intelligence
sources.supportedClaim: Creator demonstrations of a pretrained world backbone with task/embodiment policy decoders, including frozen-backbone reuse.

sources.title: Assran et al. V-JEPA 2
sources.supportedClaim: V-JEPA 2-AC learns an action-conditioned predictor over a frozen video encoder and demonstrates goal-conditioned robot planning.

sources.title: Zholus et al. RoboJEPA
sources.supportedClaim: Action-conditioned predictors scale to 8B, real robot planning takes seconds on multiple GPUs, and an optional decoder renders latent futures.

sources.title: AMI Labs. Official research direction
sources.supportedClaim: Yann LeCun is a founder; stated direction uses abstract predictive representations of camera and other sensor data. Research position rather than independent proof of universal efficiency.

sources.title: Cui et al. JEPA-Anything
sources.supportedClaim: A shared predictive learning framework instantiated in seven domains with domain-specific adapters, encoders and context-target choices, distinguishing representation and operational modes.
reviewedSections: 2.4 Shared Predictive Pretraining and Task-Specific Readout

sources.title: Zhu and Choromanska. Self-Supervised JEPA-based World Models for LiDAR Occupancy Completion and Forecasting
sources.supportedClaim: AD-LiST-JEPA learns point-cloud representations evaluated for occupancy completion and forecasting; no claimed complete autonomous controller.

sources.title: DeepSeek-AI. DeepSeek-R1
sources.supportedClaim: Large-scale reinforcement learning can improve LLM reasoning after pretraining; rewards guide learning from attempted solutions.

sources.title: Kevin Lu and Thinking Machines Lab. On-Policy Distillation
sources.supportedClaim: Student-generated trajectories are evaluated using teacher guidance for on-policy post-training. No universal performance or compute-efficiency claim is made.
